title: The Log Lady in Into The Wood is the crossroads where my two greatest...
transcript: So I think Steven Sondheim is the greatest American musical theater composer to ever live. And I think David Lynch is the greatest American surrealist to ever live. So imagine my shock and awe when I found out that Catherine Coulson, the Log Lady from Twin Peaks, and one of David Lynch's oldest and most faithful collaborators, played Milky White in a production of into the Woods. And I have not been able to find a bootleg of it. Look at her. Look at her as milky white. It's so cute. I will meet Satan at the crossroads tonight and sell my soul if Satan gave me a flash drive with a bootleg of Catherine, the Log Lady as Milky White and Steven Sondheim's Into the Woods. So ring me up, Satan. I'm ready to make the deal. And this is not the only David Lynch Twin Peaks Stephen Sondheim crossover. David Patrick Kelly, who played Jerry Horne in Twin Peaks. You dance, Jerry Horne! You dance! David Patrick Kelly. Come on. Also played the narrator in the last Broadway revival of into the Woods. But we have videos of Jerry Horne and into the Woods. Videos of the Log Lady and into the Woods have yet to surface. And I need that to happen for my sanity and my happiness. And who's that dancing with David Patrick Kelly but Richard Beemer, who plays his brother in the show. Who played Tony in the West Side Story movie. That Steven Sondheim wrote lyrics for and who was Tony's best friend in the West Side Story movie. Russ Tamblyn as riff, who plays Doctor Jacoby in Twin Peaks. Can we just have 15 seconds of Doctor Jacoby and Twin Peaks the return, please? We're sheep to these monsters, and they don't give a shit. We grow our wool, and just when we're getting warm, they come along with their electric clippers and shear our wool off. And we're just naked, screaming little fucks. No will for us. You bet your ass, Doctor Jacoby. I hate when actors call their performances brave, because very rarely is a performance brave. I can count on one hand, really, three fingers. Acting performances that I think were brave. Because, frankly, actors, usually, you're performing somebody else's work and somebody else's directions and somebody else's costumes and somebody else's set under somebody else's lighting. You do your part, and you do your part well. But I couldn't call it brave. But Catherine's performance in Twin Peaks the return that she filmed about three days before she passed away. Is one of the bravest, most moving, most awe inspiring acting performances of all time. And every time I see it, I cannot believe the bravery that she had to do that performance at that point. That all being said, I will do anything to see Catherine the Log Lady from Twin Peaks in Stephen Sondheim's into the Woods as milky white. I need the universe to do This for me
